title: Does Physics Live in the Activations? Localizing Physical Quantities in Video Diffusion Models

project_script_read.scope: Static browser visualization of Table B.2, not probe fitting or transfer evaluation code.

training_boundary: Three frozen video DiTs; new ridge probes are supervised by synthetic physical labels. Target-scene affine transfer calibration uses ten labelled target videos. No backbone training or fine-tuning is performed for the study.

hardware_and_compute.basis: No explicit hardware configuration or quantitative compute budget found in the complete paper. Acknowledgments name PLGrid, WCSS and LEONARDO allocations.
derived_not_measured: 14B parameters at two bytes per parameter require about 28 GB for weights alone; not a GPU-memory requirement.

implementation_caveats: Main probes use forward-noised labelled videos and a single denoising pass, not the models own sampling trajectories.

High linear decodability establishes readout accessibility, not factorized explicit state or physical law implementation. Weak pooled input baselines cannot establish absence of all physical information in the complete input.
ROI centers and projected radii are simulator-provided. Mass is tied to rendered radius through a constant-density relation.
Single token-frames include temporally compressed information, and DiT attention sees the complete clip; anticipation probes are not past-only prediction tests.

Cross-scene results include ten-video target-label affine calibration; calibration-versus-test isolation is not sufficiently specified in the accessible paper, and no experiment code is available to resolve it.
Only left-versus-right rolling direction steering was demonstrated; pooled high-score probes fail as broadcast steering vectors.

Table C.1 states 52 seeds but reports CogVideoX prompt flip ratio 0.017, which cannot be obtained as one integer count divided by 52. Values are quoted as reported, and the exact denominator or aggregation remains unresolved.
Reversed steering produces zero rightward flips but leaves only 0.77/0.50/0.33 of videos classified left, so zero flips does not establish preserved generation quality.
Source code is not publicly linked; standardized-to-raw weight conversion, practical SLERP norm handling, and hyperparameter selection remain unaudited.
